sources.title: Contrastive Learning: How Models Learn by Comparison
sources.snippet: Contrastive learning is a way to train models by showing them pairs of examples and teaching them what's similar and what's different. Instead of using labeled data, the model learns from the structure of the data itself. Over time, it builds representations that group similar things together and separate dissimilar ones.
